{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && cat > specs/001-transactions/checklists/requirements.md <<'CHK_EOF'
# Specification Quality Checklist: Atomic Batch Transactions for TinyDB

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

## Content Quality

- [x] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
  - Note: The spec names the public capability (`apply`, `ValueError`, `db.table('_default')` handles) because the frozen requirements R01-R03 define the observable contract in those terms; storage internals, algorithms, and file layout are not prescribed. This is the contract boundary, not an implementation design.
- [x] Focused on user value and business needs
- [x] Written for non-technical stakeholders (Given/When/Then scenarios; requirement language)
- [x] All mandatory sections completed

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain (verified: `grep -c 'NEEDS CLARIFICATION'` -> 0)
- [x] Requirements are testable and unambiguous (FR-001..FR-009 each name concrete inputs/outputs/errors)
- [x] Success criteria are measurable (SC-001..SC-005 use 100%/zero counts and named suites)
- [x] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no storage or algorithm details)
- [x] All acceptance scenarios are defined (3 user stories, 10 Given/When/Then scenarios)
- [x] Edge cases are identified (malformed ops, missing target, empty batch, interleaved use, nested data, pre-existing handles)
- [x] Scope is clearly bounded (default table only; additive; no cross-table transactions)
- [x] Dependencies and assumptions identified (Assumptions section, 6 items)

## Feature Readiness

- [x] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria (FR-001->US1/US3, FR-002/003/004->US1+Edge Cases, FR-005/006/007->US2, FR-008/009->US3)
- [x] User scenarios cover primary flows (apply, atomic rollback, transparency/aliasing)
- [x] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
- [x] No implementation details leak into specification (contract-level names only, per note above)

## Notes

- All items pass on the first validation iteration; no spec updates were required.
- No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers were needed: every ambiguous point has a reasonable default, recorded in Assumptions.
- Ready for `$speckit-plan`.
CHK_EOF
echo WROTE_CHECKLIST; ls -R specs/001-transactions"}
